endorsements.quote: At the practice level, every locally deployed model should have a model card recording the weights identifier, quantization, hardware, deployment date, intended use, validation dataset, and contraindications, plus an audit log capturing prompts, outputs, clinician overrides, and adverse events.
Local deployment shifts the locus of risk from external transmission to internal governance, and practices must design access controls, audit trails, and prompt-logging policies to match [ 36 ].

Practices should therefore (1) prefer the highest-precision variant their hardware supports for clinical tasks, (2) validate the specific quantized variant they deploy on dermatology-relevant prompts before clinical use, and (3) revalidate when changing quantization formats or hardware.

unlisted_practices: Prefer retrieval-augmented generation over the LLM's parametric memory for downstream queries of clinical documentation.
Integrate mandatory human-in-the-loop validation protocols into all clinical AI deployments.
Select a model size that matches available local hardware.
Fine-tune open-weight models on locally curated, demographically representative datasets to address population-specific performance gaps.
Audit open-weight models for bias through stratified accuracy testing across Fitzpatrick skin types.
Use federated learning across institutions to broaden representation without centralizing sensitive imaging data.
Host opt-in regional or consortium registries that aggregate model cards and adverse event signals from local deployments.
Incorporate reporting frameworks such as CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and TRIPOD+AI into practice protocols for local deployments.
Apply automated PII scrubbing and face blurring to total-body photographs in local AI pipelines.
Do not assume model compression yields equivalent performance across all use cases without empirical validation.
